vocalizationCorrections.reason: Restore the verbal noun تلبّس, qualification by the concepts; the source consonants are unchanged.

Retain the early/base consonants المشخص but vocalize them passively: the subject is individuated, not an individuator. The adjective is genitive after بالموضوع; الأعراض begins the following nominal clause and is nominative. The punctuation separates the clauses. proposedEditorialNotes.text: At 1428 vol.1 p.182 n.3, the editor explains that specific form is not an efficient cause here in the sense of independently bestowing existence. He quotes a pupil of the author who reads “prior to it” as priority in causation, not priority in time. The main text of both editions retains the author’s formulation; this note attributes the clarification to the later commentary.

unadoptedVariants.decision: Retain the early/base consequential conjunction; both constructions carry the same proof.

unadoptedVariants.laterNoteText: وفي النسخ : «السؤال عنه». وما أثبتناه هو الصحيح.
unadoptedVariants.decision: Retain the singular question about the newly constructed building, an explicit masculine antecedent بناء. The later dual refers instead to clay and stone and is an optional anaphoric clarification, unlike the adopted إليها/إليهما correction.
Retain the early/base reading and the English property. The later unfootnoted form is recorded but does not justify silently replacing the authorial formulation.
Retain early consonants and read passive المشخَّصِ; the existing English individuated already gives that coherent sense. Do not import the later added tāʾ.

argumentFindings: All21 Arabic and17 English paragraphs are accounted for. Both proofs, both first-proof objections, the individual-form objection, the complete conclusion, and both stated consequences are present.

The conclusion distinguishes the dependence of secondary matter on specific form from corporeal form’s partnership in preserving prime matter. The English preserves causal priority and the replacement of corporeality with specific form; it does not assert temporal priority.
The first objection’s singular question can refer to بناء. A dual correction is not automatically obligatory merely because the later editor prints one.
No original authorial footnote or quotation locator was omitted from this chapter. Later references to Suhrawardī, Ṣadrā, Ibn Sīnā and Bahmanyār are editor apparatus.

editorialCommentary.finding: The later editor identifies Peripatetic and Illuminationist positions, cites the proofs and objections in Ṣadrā, Ibn Sīnā and Bahmanyār, and explicates the examples. These attributions are not added authorial sentences.

At182n3, the editor says efficient cause here does not mean a separate bestower of existence and quotes a pupil interpreting the priority as causal, not temporal. At183n1 he cross-refers to his earlier disagreement on matter/form priority.

editorialCommentary.finding: The priority of quantity, bibliography of the definitions, and Sabzawārī’s clarification that the intended division is conceptual rather than destructive are later editor commentary.

The editor cites Bidāya p99 for the division definition, reproduces al-Taftāzānī’s distinction between potential division and the wider supposition of distinct parts, and gives al-Rāzī’s reply that sensible equality may define an intellectually abstract quantity. These are objections and replies in apparatus, not missing author body.

englishCorrections.old: Discrete quantity, namely number, necessarily exists externally.
englishCorrections.new: Discrete quantity, namely number, self-evidently exists externally.
englishCorrections.reason: بالضرورة marks the asserted evident status of this existence claim. “Necessarily exists” can wrongly suggest the intrinsic necessary existence of an accidental quantity. Preserve the source’s epistemic claim without turning it into ontological necessity.

englishCorrections.old: because there is a common measure among its instances.
englishCorrections.new: because there is a common measure among their instances.
englishCorrections.reason: Preserve the early/base feminine أفرادها, whose nearest grammatical antecedent is the several kinds of motions. The current English singular its tacitly follows the later masculine أفراده referring to time. Their keeps the early reference to instances of those motions; disclose the later alternative separately.

orthographicCorrections.reason: Remove the spurious shadda on yāʾ in finite; consonants unchanged.
Move shadda from kāf to ʿayn in cube; both editions name the cube at this locus.

vocalizationCorrections.reason: The numeral is genitive after إلى and in construct with أجزاء, so it is neither accusative nor nunated. No decisive external case vowel is claimed.
قوة is the nominative predicate of إنّ كلّ جزء, not an accusative object; external consonants are unchanged.

proposedEditorialNotes.text: The 1428 editor at vol.1 p.186 n.2 objects to the author’s middle-segment example. He prefers Sabzawārī’s examples of a point between parts of a line, a line between parts of a surface, a surface between parts of a body, and an instant between parts of time. He argues that a middle piece does not distinguish continuous from discrete quantity, since a middle unit could similarly be selected in seven. Both editions retain the author’s example in the body; this is an attributed philosophical objection, not an attested replacement.

At 1428 vol.1 p.188 n.2, the editor quotes a pupil of the author who disputes the final claim about irregular figures. The objection is that an irregular figure may be one actual shape; imagining its partition for calculation does not establish actual composition, any more than imagining two triangles makes a square actually composite. Both editions retain the author’s conclusion. This note reports the objection without silently substituting it for the source text.

unadoptedVariants.decision: Retain ذا under the continuing government of يكون. Later ذو can begin a separate nominal clause, but there is no need to replace the coherent early grammar.

Retain the early feminine referring to the preceding motions. The later masculine instead makes time explicit as antecedent; align English their with the retained early reading and record the alternative.

argumentFindings: All18 Arabic and8 English paragraphs are accounted for. The middle-segment example, four/six reductio for a common number-boundary, temporal actuality/potentiality claim, external-existence discussion, conditional status of line, and final irregular-figure classification are retained.
Do not silently correct the author’s geometry: the later edition retains both disputed examples in the body and places objections in notes.
The claim about number’s external existence is treated as epistemic necessity/self-evidence, not an additional assertion of intrinsic necessary existence.
No original author footnote or original citation locator is missing. Early111 clearly shows the end of VI9 followed by the tenth-chapter heading; later188 ends the chapter before189.

editorialCommentary.finding: The editor at n2 objects to treating a middle segment as a common boundary and prefers Sabzawārī’s point/line, line/surface, surface/body and instant/time examples; he argues that the author’s construction would also work for the middle unit of seven.
Later notes identify the quantity terminology, the reported disagreement of theologians about numbers/magnitudes, and the promised proof of time at IX11. These attributions do not change the body.

Later n1 attributes distinct number-species to Aristotle/Ibn Sīnā and the majority report in Ṣadrā. Later n2 quotes an author’s pupil objecting that hypothetical partition of an irregular shape does not establish actual composition.
